001package io.github.ai4ci;
002
003import java.io.IOException;
004import java.nio.file.Files;
005import java.nio.file.Path;
006
007import org.apache.logging.log4j.Level;
008import org.apache.logging.log4j.core.Layout;
009import org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.ConsoleAppender;
010import org.apache.logging.log4j.core.appender.FileAppender;
011import org.apache.logging.log4j.core.config.Configurator;
012import org.apache.logging.log4j.core.config.NullConfiguration;
013import org.apache.logging.log4j.core.layout.PatternLayout;
014import org.slf4j.Logger;
015import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
016
017import io.github.ai4ci.config.ExperimentConfiguration;
018
019/**
020 * Logging setup helper that adapts the logging sinks depending on whether the
021 * simulator is running inside a SLURM batch job or interactively.
022 *
023 * <p>
024 * Rationale for routing logging to console when running under SLURM:
025 * <ul>
026 * <li>SLURM captures and manages the stdout/stderr streams for each job/task
027 * and stores them in job-specific files (e.g. <code>slurm-{jobid}.out</code>).
028 * Writing to the console ensures that a single canonical per-task log file is
029 * produced by the scheduler rather than having several processes write
030 * concurrently to a shared log file on a network filesystem.</li>
031 * <li>Using console output avoids contention and atomicity issues that can
032 * arise when multiple parallel tasks attempt to append to the same file (which
033 * may be on NFS), and reduces the need for additional file locking logic inside
034 * the application.</li>
035 * <li>Scheduler-captured logs are easier to aggregate, view, and associate with
036 * a particular job or array task when debugging or post-processing. It also
037 * preserves SLURM-provided job metadata (timestamps, job id) together with the
038 * application output.</li>
039 * <li>When running interactively (not under SLURM), a file appender is created
040 * so logs are written to a consistent location inside the experiment
041 * <code>batchDirectory</code>. This makes it easy to inspect logs from local
042 * development runs.</li>
043 * </ul>
044 *
045 * <p>
046 * Behaviour summary:
047 * <ul>
048 * <li>If <code>cfg.getBatchConfig().isSlurmBatch()</code> is true, the logger
049 * configures a console appender only; SLURM (or whatever batch system is in
050 * use) is expected to capture that output into its per-job files.</li>
051 * <li>If not running under a SLURM batch, a FileAppender is also created and an
052 * existing <code>jpansim2.log</code> file in the batch directory is removed
053 * before starting to keep local runs tidy.</li>
054 * </ul>
055 */
056public class SlurmAwareLogger {
057
058        static Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(SlurmAwareLogger.class);
059
060        /**
061         * Configure logging for the experiment run.
062         *
063         * <p>
064         * This method creates a <b>console</b> appender in all cases and will add a
065         * <b>file</b> appender only when
066         * <code>cfg.getBatchConfig().isSlurmBatch()</code> is false. The console
067         * appender is intentionally used when running under SLURM so that the
068         * scheduler can capture the complete per-task output in its job files. See
069         * class-level Javadoc for rationale.
070         *
071         * @param cfg           the experiment configuration (used to determine batch
072         *                      mode and names)
073         * @param baseDirectory the experiment base/batch directory where local logs
074         *                      are written
075         * @param console       the log level to use for the console appender
076         * @param file          the log level to use for the file appender (only used
077         *                      when not running under SLURM)
078         */
079        public static void setupLogger(
080                        ExperimentConfiguration cfg, Path baseDirectory, Level console,
081                        Level file
082        ) {
083
084                var batchDirectory = cfg.getBatchDirectoryPath(baseDirectory);
085
086                var ctx = Configurator.initialize(new NullConfiguration());
087                var config = ctx.getConfiguration();
088                config.getAppenders()
089                        .forEach(
090                                (key, value) -> config.getRootLogger()
091                                        .removeAppender(value.getName())
092                        );
093
094                var pattern = String.format(
095                        "%%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS} [%s] [%%-5level] %%msg%%n",
096                        cfg.getBatchConfig()
097                                .getBatchName()
098                );
099
100                Layout<?> layout = PatternLayout.newBuilder()
101                        .withPattern(pattern)
102                        .withConfiguration(config)
103                        .build();
104
105                // Console Appender — always configured; SLURM captures stdout/stderr
106                var consoleAppender = ConsoleAppender.newBuilder()
107                        .setName("ConsoleAppender")
108                        .setLayout(layout)
109                        .build();
110
111                consoleAppender.start();
112                config.addAppender(consoleAppender);
113
114                var rootLogger = config
115                        .getLoggerConfig(org.apache.logging.log4j.LogManager.ROOT_LOGGER_NAME);
116                rootLogger.setLevel(Level.DEBUG);
117                rootLogger.addAppender(consoleAppender, console, null);
118
119                if (!cfg.getBatchConfig()
120                        .isSlurmBatch()) {
121
122                        // File Appender only if SLURM not running otherwise console output
123                        // is directed to file by SLURM. Writing a local per-run file is useful
124                        // for interactive development and reproducible local debugging.
125
126                        var logFileName = batchDirectory.resolve("jpansim2.log")
127                                .toString();
128                        try {
129                                Files.deleteIfExists(batchDirectory.resolve("jpansim2.log"));
130                        } catch (IOException e) {
131                                System.out
132                                        .println("Problem deleting old log files: " + e.getMessage());
133                        }
134
135                        var fileAppender = FileAppender.newBuilder()
136                                .withFileName(logFileName)
137                                .setName("FileAppender")
138                                .setLayout(layout)
139                                .build();
140
141                        fileAppender.start();
142                        config.addAppender(fileAppender);
143                        rootLogger.addAppender(fileAppender, file, null);
144                }
145
146                ctx.updateLoggers();
147                log.info("Bootstrapping logger.");
148                log.info(
149                        "Starting batch: " + cfg.getBatchConfig()
150                                .getBatchName()
151                );
152                log.info(
153                        "Batch model configurations: " + cfg.getBatchSetupList()
154                                .size()
155                );
156                log.info(
157                        "Executions per model: " + cfg.getExecution()
158                                .size()
159                );
160        }
161}
